newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss may ease foreign property ownership laws.
newsitem.headline: Swiss may ease foreign property ownership laws.

text.p: The Swiss cabinet intends to propose to parliament a list of revisions to existing laws governing foreign property ownership with the aim of boosting investment in Switzerland, the Justice Department said.
The proposals would be part of an earlier-announced government investment programme.

The revisions, if passed into law, would remove approval requirements for foreigners seeking to purchase properties for industrial, business or service activities, the Justice Department statement said.

Under the proposal, approvals for purchases of partial interests in companies involved in such business activities would also be done away with along with approval requirements for the purchase of homes to be used as primary domiciles by employees of foreign companies operating in Switzerland.
These steps would give foreign investors the chance to create new production and service organisations and thus help reduce Swiss unemployment, the statement said.

However, it said the cabinet made no proposal to ease restrictions on the foreign purchase of vacation homes, a measure which was rejected by Swiss voters in June 1995 referendum, the Justice Department also said. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
